anxiety.answer: A duʿā the Prophet used to say against worry is "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, and from being overcome by debt and overpowered by men." It is recorded in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6369 and graded ṣaḥīḥ.
faq: What duʿā should I read for anxiety?

Start with the refuge from worry and grief in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6369. Anas said the Prophet said it constantly. If distress is acute rather than constant, Bukhārī 6345 is the one said at the moment something presses down on you.
Is there a Qurʾanic verse for anxiety?
Yes. The duʿā of Yūnus, said from inside the whale, is in the Qurʾan at 21:87, and the hadith says no Muslim ever supplicates with it for anything without being answered.
How do I know these duʿās are authentic?
Every entry on this page shows its collection, its number and its grading. Nothing appears unless the Arabic matches the primary source word for word and the grading rule passes.

sadness.answer: For grief the Prophet asked refuge from hamm and ḥazan together, worry about what is coming and sorrow about what has gone, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6369. For bereavement specifically the Qurʾan gives the words said at the moment of loss, at 2:156 to 157.
faq: What do you say when you are sad?
The refuge from worry and grief in Bukhārī 6369 is narrated as one he used to say. It names sorrow about the past and dread about the future as two separate things and asks refuge from both.
What is the duʿā when someone dies?
Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn, from Qurʾan 2:156. Umm Salamah was taught to follow it with a request to be rewarded in the loss and given something better after it.
Does Islam allow you to grieve?
Yes. Holding his dying son, the Prophet said the eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what our Lord is pleased with. Tears and sorrow are permitted; what is said aloud is what is held.

debt.answer: The duʿā taught for debt is "O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me free of need of anyone besides You." It was given to a man who owed more than he could pay, in Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3563, graded ḥasan.
faq: What duʿā do I read when I am in debt?
Tirmidhī 3563 is the one taught specifically for it. ʿAli gave it to a man in debt and told him that if he owed a mountain of gold, Allah would settle it for him.
Is there a Qurʾanic verse about debt and hardship?
Qurʾan 65:2 to 3 promises a way out and provision from where a person does not expect. It is on this page with the full passage and translation.
Should I still ask people for help?
The duʿā asks to be made free of need of anyone besides Allah, which is about dependence rather than about refusing help. The Prophet also sought refuge from being overcome by debt, in Bukhārī 6369.

illness.answer: For pain in your own body, put your hand where it hurts and say bismillāh three times, then "I seek refuge in the might of Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear" seven times. It is in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 5737, graded ṣaḥīḥ.
faq: What duʿā do I say when I am ill?
Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 5737 gives the words and the action together: the right hand on the place that hurts, and the refuge said seven times. ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ said it and reported that Allah healed him.
What do I say when visiting someone sick?
The Prophet said over a sick person: take away the harm, Lord of people, heal, for You are the Healer, a healing that leaves no illness behind. It is in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5675.
Does making duʿā mean I should not see a doctor?

No. When bedouins asked whether seeking treatment was allowed, the answer was an instruction, not a permission: seek treatment, servants of Allah, for Allah has put down no disease without a cure with it.

forgiveness.answer: The Prophet called one supplication the chief of the ways of asking forgiveness: "O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant. I am on Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able." Whoever says it and dies that day enters the Garden. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5070.
faq: What is the best duʿā for forgiveness?
Sayyid al-istighfār, in Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5070. Its honest clause is in the middle: as much as I am able. It does not claim the covenant was kept.
What if I keep committing the same sin?

A hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 7507 describes a servant who sinned three times and was forgiven each time. What qualified him was not the remorse but knowing he has a Lord who both forgives and holds to account.
Is any sin too big to forgive?
Qurʾan 39:53 tells those who have wronged themselves not to despair of the mercy of Allah, who forgives all sins. The full verse and translation are on this page.

travel.answer: Setting out, the Prophet said Allāhu akbar three times, then "Glory to the One who made this subservient to us, for we could never have managed it. And to our Lord we are returning." It continues with a request for goodness and mindfulness on the road. Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 3275.
faq: What is the duʿā for travelling?
Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 3275 gives the full travel duʿā, said once seated on the transport. It asks for righteousness and mindfulness on the journey before it asks for the journey to be easy.
What do I say when leaving the house?
Bismillāh, I rely on Allah, there is no power and no strength except with Allah. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5095 says it is said as you step out, and that the one who says it is guarded and guided.
Is there a duʿā for coming home safely?
Yes. The Prophet sought refuge from the hardship of the journey, the gloom of the return, and an ugly sight in property and family, in Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik 1796.

fear.answer: When the odds are against you, the words the Qurʾan records at 3:173 are ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿma-l-wakīl: Allah is enough for us, and what an excellent guardian. If a specific person frightens you, Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1537 gives the duʿā the Prophet said when he feared a people: O Allah, we place You before them.
faq: What do I read when I am afraid?
Ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿma-l-wakīl, from Qurʾan 3:173. The Prophet also gave it to companions frightened by the warning about the horn, telling them to say it in Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 2431.
Is there a duʿā when you fear a particular person?
Yes. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1537: O Allah, we place You before them, and we seek refuge in You from their evil. It was said when facing a group he feared.
Does duʿā replace taking precautions?
No. The camel was still to be tied. These supplications are for what remains after you have done what you can, which is why 3:173 is said by people who had already been through Uḥud.

anger.answer: The Prophet watched two men insulting each other, one of them red in the face, and said he knew a word that would take away what the man was feeling: aʿūdhu billāhi mina-sh-shayṭāni-r-rajīm, I seek refuge in Allah from the rejected Satan. It is in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3282 and 6115.
faq: What duʿā calms anger?
The refuge from Satan, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6115. In that narration the man was too far into his anger to take the way out, which is part of why it is worth saying early.
Is there anything else to do when angry?
The site carries the related guidance from the same chapters, including the instruction not to pray against your own children or household in a moment of temper, in Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1532.
Why seek refuge rather than ask for calm?
The wording treats anger as something arriving from outside rather than as a mood to be managed. That is the framing the hadith itself uses.

loneliness.answer: For loneliness the Qurʾan gives words for wanting people around you: rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyun, our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of eyes, at 25:74. Alongside it, ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿma-l-wakīl at 3:173 was said by people who had been left on their own.
faq: Is there a duʿā for loneliness?
Qurʾan 25:74 asks for family and companionship directly. For the feeling of being unsupported, 3:173 is the passage said by those who had been abandoned and answered that Allah was enough.
What did the Prophet say about being alone?
ʿAlqama arrived in a strange city, prayed two units and asked Allah to make easy for him someone to sit with, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6278. The duʿā is on this page.
Does this page include verses as well as hadith?
Yes. Every entry names whether it is Qurʾan or hadith, gives the reference, and for hadith shows the authenticity grading.

despair.answer: The duʿā of Yūnus, said from inside the whale, is the one narrated for hopelessness: lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu mina-ẓ-ẓālimīn. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3505 reports that no Muslim ever supplicates with it for anything without being answered. It is graded ṣaḥīḥ.
faq: What duʿā do I make when I feel hopeless?
The duʿā of Yūnus, Tirmidhī 3505. It contains no request at all, only an acknowledgement, which is part of why it is cited for situations that feel closed.
Is there a verse for despair?
Qurʾan 39:53 addresses those who have wronged themselves and tells them not to despair of the mercy of Allah, who forgives all sins.
What if I feel I have gone too far?
A hadith in Sunan an-Nasāʾī 2080 describes a man who asked to be burnt and scattered so Allah could not find him, and was forgiven for the fear that drove it.

overwhelm.answer: For carrying more than you think you can hold, the verse is Qurʾan 2:286: lā yukallifu-llāhu nafsan illā wusʿahā, Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It ends with the duʿā the companions were taught to answer it with: our Lord, do not lay on us a burden like the one You laid on those before us.
faq: What do I read when I feel I cannot cope?
Qurʾan 2:286. The verse states the limit and then gives you the words to say back: do not burden us beyond our strength, pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us.
Is there a duʿā for when it does not let up?
Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3524 is the one narrated for something wearing you down, and Qurʾan 94:5 to 6 states twice that ease comes with hardship, not after it.
What is the difference between this and severe distress?
This page is for a load carried over time. If you are in an acute moment where everything presses in at once, the supplication narrated for that is on the severe distress page.

gratitude.answer: Qurʾan 14:7 states the promise plainly: if you are grateful, I will surely increase you. For the moment something good happens, the site carries the supplications of thanks the Prophet used, each with its source and grading shown.
faq: What do you say when something good happens?
Alḥamdulillāh, and the fuller forms narrated for it. Qurʾan 14:7 is the verse that ties gratitude to increase, and it is on this page with the full passage.
Is there a duʿā for a blessing you are afraid of losing?
Yes. Qurʾan 18:39 records the words said on entering a garden: mā shāʾa-llāhu lā quwwata illā billāh.
What if I do not feel grateful?
The hadith carried here treat gratitude as an act rather than a feeling. Saying it is the practice; the feeling is not a precondition.

envy.answer: Against envy, whether you feel it or fear it from others, the Qurʾan gives Surah al-Falaq at 113:1 to 5, which names the envier explicitly: min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad. The Prophet said of al-Falaq and an-Nās that no one has ever sought refuge with anything like them.
faq: What duʿā protects against envy?
Surah al-Falaq, Qurʾan 113. Its final clause asks refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies, which is the only place envy is named directly in the two protective surahs.
What do I say if I feel envy myself?
The instruction narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6490 is to look at the one below you rather than the one above. It does not say stop looking, only look both ways.
How often should the protective surahs be read?
The narrations on this page give the times they were said, including morning and evening and before sleep, each with its reference.

shame.answer: For guilt the Prophet called one supplication the chief of the ways of asking forgiveness, sayyid al-istighfār, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6306. Whoever says it in the day with certainty and dies before evening enters the Garden. Its honest clause sits in the middle: I am on Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able.
faq: What duʿā removes guilt?
Sayyid al-istighfār, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6306. It does not claim the covenant was kept, which is why it is the one narrated for people who know they have fallen short.
What if I have done something I cannot say out loud?

Bukhārī 6070 describes the private conversation on the Day of Resurrection where a servant is made to admit everything and then told: I covered it for you in the world, and today I forgive it for you.
Is there a limit to how often I can repent?
Bukhārī 7507 records a servant who sinned three times and was forgiven each time, with the same reason given each time.

distress.answer: For acute distress the narration is Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6345, said at the time of karb: three statements naming Allah as the Magnificent, the Forbearing, Lord of the mighty Throne, Lord of the heavens and the earth. Ibn ʿAbbās reports it as what was said at that moment, with nothing asked for.
faq: What is the duʿā at a time of severe distress?
Bukhārī 6345. Karb is distress that presses on the chest, and the supplication is three declarations rather than a request.
Is there a duʿā for a situation that feels closed?
The duʿā of Yūnus, Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3505, said from inside the whale, is the one narrated with the promise that whoever supplicates with it is answered.
Can I say these in English?
The Arabic is given with transliteration and translation on every entry so you can say it in either. The site shows the source and grading for each.

someone-ill.answer: Visiting someone ill, the Prophet said seven times: asʾalu-llāha-l-ʿaẓīma rabba-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīmi an yashfiyak, I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to cure you. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 2083 adds that if the person's time has not come, they are relieved of that illness.
faq: What do you say when visiting a sick person?
Tirmidhī 2083, said seven times. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5675 gives the other narrated wording: take away the harm, Lord of people, a healing that leaves no illness behind.
What do you say to comfort them?
Lā baʾsa ṭahūrun in shāʾa-llāh, no harm, it is a cleansing, if Allah wills. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3616.
Does visiting the sick have its own reward?
Yes, and the narrations on it are carried here with their references and gradings.

death.answer: At the moment of loss the Qurʾan gives the words at 2:156: innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. Umm Salamah was taught to follow them with a request to be rewarded in the affliction and given something better after it, and she reported the ending herself.
faq: What do you say when someone dies?
Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn, Qurʾan 2:156, then the request recorded in Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik 561 to be rewarded in the loss and given better after it.
What is the duʿā at a funeral prayer?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 3201 gives the wording that covers the living and the dead, the young and the old, the present and the absent. It is on this page in full.
Is grief itself allowed?
Yes. Holding his dying son the Prophet said the eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what our Lord is pleased with. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 3126.

poverty.answer: When provision is tight, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6889 carries the request to have debt settled and to be freed from poverty. For debt specifically, Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3563 gives the duʿā taught to a man who owed more than he could pay: suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden.
faq: What duʿā do I make for money?
Tirmidhī 3563 for debt, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6889 for provision generally. Both are on this page with the Arabic, transliteration, translation and grading.
Is it wrong to ask Allah for wealth?
The Prophet made duʿā for Anas asking for wealth and children and blessing in them, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 1982. The third clause, blessing, is the one usually left off.
What did the Prophet say about wealth itself?
That it is green and sweet, and that whoever takes it with a contented heart is blessed in it while whoever takes it with a craving heart is not. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6441.

oppression.answer: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 2448 records the warning: beware the supplication of the one who has been wronged, for there is no veil between it and Allah. The Qurʾan at 14:42 adds that Allah is never unaware of what wrongdoers do, only delaying them to a day when eyes will stare.
faq: Is the duʿā of a wronged person answered?
The narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 2448 says there is no veil between it and Allah. It was said to Muʿādh when he was sent to Yemen, as a caution to the one holding authority.
What if the person who wronged me got away with it?
Qurʾan 14:42 addresses exactly that: Allah is not unaware, only delaying them to a day when eyes will stare, fixed open.
Should I make duʿā against them?

The material here includes the counterweight: the Prophet was naming three men at Uḥud when the verse came down that none of the matter was his, and all three later accepted Islam. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3004.

enemy.answer: Facing people who mean you harm, Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1537 gives the wording: Allāhumma innā najʿaluka fī nuḥūrihim wa naʿūdhu bika min shurūrihim, O Allah, we place You before them and seek refuge in You from their evil. Qurʾan 3:173 adds ḥasbunallāhu wa niʿma-l-wakīl.
faq: What duʿā do I say against an enemy?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1537. It does not ask for harm; it asks for Allah to be placed between you and them, and for refuge from what they intend.
Is there a verse for when people gather against you?
Qurʾan 3:173, said by people who had been told an army was massing, and who answered that Allah is enough for us and an excellent guardian.
Should I pray for their harm?
The narrations carried here weigh against it, including Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3908, where the Prophet asked that the later generations of a hostile tribe be given bounty rather than punishment.

failure.answer: When something did not go the way you wanted, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6774 gives the wording: qadaru-llāhi wa mā shāʾa faʿal, it is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills, and warns that saying if only opens the door to regret. Qurʾan 2:216 adds that you may hate a thing and it is better for you.
faq: What do you say when things go wrong?
Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6774: it is the decree of Allah and He does what He wills. The same narration cautions against the word law, if only, because of where it leads.
Is there a verse for not getting what you wanted?
Qurʾan 2:216: perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. Allah knows and you do not.
Does this mean I should not try again?
The same narration begins by telling you to be keen on what benefits you and to seek Allah's help and not to be incapable. Acceptance comes after effort, not instead of it.

marriage.answer: For a decision about marriage the duʿā is istikhāra, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6382, which Jābir says the Prophet taught for every matter the way he taught a chapter of the Qurʾan. For a spouse and children who are a comfort, Qurʾan 25:74 gives the wording.
faq: What duʿā do I make about marriage?
Istikhāra, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6382: two units of prayer, then the supplication, naming the matter out loud at the point where it asks you to.
Is there a duʿā for a righteous spouse?
Qurʾan 25:74 asks for spouses and offspring who are a comfort of the eyes, and to be made a leader for the righteous.
What is said at a wedding?
Bāraka-llāhu lakum wa bāraka ʿalaykum wa jamaʿa baynakumā fī khayr. Sunan Ibn Mājah 1905.

children.answer: To protect children, the Prophet used the words Ibrāhīm used over Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq: uʿīdhukumā bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah, min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4737 and Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3371. For hoping for a child, Qurʾan 3:38 gives the duʿā of Zakariyyā.
faq: What duʿā protects my children?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3371. It names three things: every devil, every crawling thing, and every eye that harms.
Is there a duʿā for having a child?
Qurʾan 3:38, the words of Zakariyyā: my Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Qurʾan 25:74 and 37:100 are also on this page.
What should I avoid saying to my children?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1532 records the instruction not to pray against your children, because it may land on an hour in which giving is happening.

parents.answer: The Qurʾan gives the duʿā for parents at 17:24: rabbi-rḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā, my Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. The hadith carried here add what is owed to them while they are alive and after.
faq: What is the duʿā for parents?
Qurʾan 17:24. It ties the mercy asked for to the care they gave, which is the logic the verse itself uses.
Can I do something for a parent who has died?
The narrations here include continuing charity and supplication on their behalf, each with its reference and grading.
What is the reward for keeping family ties?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5985: whoever would like his provision widened and his trace extended should keep the ties of his kinship.

reconcile.answer: For bad feeling between people, Sunan Abī Dāwūd 969 gives the wording: Allāhumma allif bayna qulūbinā wa aṣliḥ dhāta bayninā, O Allah, join our hearts and set right what is between us. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6065 sets the limit: it is not lawful to cut off a Muslim beyond three days.
faq: What duʿā helps repair a relationship?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 969, which asks for hearts to be joined before it asks for the situation to be fixed.
How long can I stay not speaking to someone?
Three days. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4913 adds that if you greet them three times and get no reply, the other has taken the sin on themselves.
Is it allowed to say something untrue to make peace?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4920 says the one who puts things right between people, saying something good or passing on something good, is not a liar.

knowledge.answer: Before study or an exam, Qurʾan 20:114 gives the request: rabbi zidnī ʿilmā, my Lord, increase me in knowledge. For speaking under pressure, 20:25 to 28 gives the duʿā of Mūsā: expand my chest, make my task easy, and loosen the knot from my tongue.
faq: What duʿā do I read before an exam?
Qurʾan 20:114 for knowledge, and 20:25 to 28 for the nerves and the speaking. Both are on this page in full with translation.
Is there a duʿā for a bad memory?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 832 records a man who said he could not retain anything of the Qurʾan and was given five short phrases, then asked what was in it for him and was given more.
What did the Prophet say about seeking knowledge?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 71: whoever Allah wants good for, He gives understanding in the religion.

work.answer: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6889 carries the request to have debt settled and be freed from need. For the working day, Sunan Ibn Mājah 925 gives the morning supplication asking for beneficial knowledge, wholesome provision and accepted work.
faq: What duʿā is made for work and provision?
Sunan Ibn Mājah 925, said after the dawn prayer: knowledge that benefits, provision that is wholesome, and work that is accepted.
Is there a duʿā before a difficult task?
Istikhāra, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6382, for anything you are undecided about. For the task itself, Qurʾan 20:25 to 28 asks for the chest to be expanded and the task made easy.
What is said about earning?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6441 records that wealth taken with a contented heart is blessed and wealth taken with a craving heart is not.

decision.answer: For any decision, the duʿā is istikhāra: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6382. Pray two units that are not obligatory, then say it, naming the matter out loud where the wording asks you to. Jābir says it was taught for all matters the way a chapter of the Qurʾan was taught.
faq: How do I pray istikhāra?
Two units of voluntary prayer, then the supplication in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6382, naming the specific matter at the point indicated. The full Arabic and translation are on this page.
What if I get no clear feeling afterwards?
The duʿā asks for the matter to be decreed and made easy if it is good, and turned away if it is not. It asks for the outcome to be arranged, not for a feeling to be sent.
Can I pray it more than once?
The narration does not limit it. It is worded for any matter a person is concerned about.

weak-iman.answer: When faith feels unsteady, the duʿā is yā muqalliba-l-qulūbi thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik, O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3522, graded ṣaḥīḥ. Umm Salamah said he said it often, and asked him why.
faq: What duʿā strengthens faith?
Tirmidhī 3522. When Umm Salamah asked why he said it so often, he answered that no heart is not between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful.
Is it normal for faith to go up and down?
The wording of the duʿā itself assumes it. It addresses Allah as the Turner of hearts and asks for firmness rather than claiming it.
What if I have doubts?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3372 records the Prophet saying that we have more right to doubt than Ibrāhīm, who asked to be shown how the dead are raised.

waswas.answer: For intrusive thoughts about faith, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 340 records the companions describing thoughts too terrible to speak, and the answer: dhālika ṣarīḥu-l-īmān, that is clear faith. Being disturbed by the thought is itself the sign. Surah an-Nās, Qurʾan 114, is the refuge named for whispering.
faq: Are intrusive thoughts about religion sinful?
Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 340 treats distress at the thought as evidence of faith rather than of its absence. The companions asked and were told that is clear faith.
What do I say when they come?
Surah an-Nās, Qurʾan 114, which names the whisperer who withdraws. The narrations here also record seeking refuge and turning away rather than arguing with the thought.
Should I try to reason them out?
The guidance carried here is to seek refuge and move on rather than engage, which is the pattern the narrations describe.

steadfastness.answer: Qurʾan 94:5 to 6 states it twice: fa-inna maʿa-l-ʿusri yusrā, inna maʿa-l-ʿusri yusrā. With hardship comes ease, said once and then said again. The hadith on this page add what to say while the hardship is still running.
faq: What verse helps when hardship is long?
Qurʾan 94:5 to 6. The repetition is in the text itself, not an emphasis added later.
What duʿā is made for patience?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6470 records that whoever tries to be patient, Allah gives him patience, and that no gift is better or wider than patience.
Is there a reward for the first moment?
Sunan Ibn Mājah 1597: if you are patient and seek the reward at the first blow, I will not be satisfied with any reward for you short of the Garden.

death-remembrance.answer: Passing a graveyard, the Prophet said: as-salāmu ʿalaykum ahla-d-diyāri mina-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muslimīn, wa innā in shāʾa-llāhu bikum lāḥiqūn. Peace be upon you, people of these dwellings, and we will be joining you. Sunan an-Nasāʾī 2040.
faq: What do you say when visiting a grave?
Sunan an-Nasāʾī 2040. The greeting is addressed to the people there, and ends by saying that we will follow.
What is said at a burial?
Bismillāhi wa ʿalā sunnati rasūli-llāh, said as the body is placed in. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 3213.
Why remember death at all?
The narrations here treat it as a corrective to long hope. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6420 notes that the heart of an old man stays young in two things: love of the world and long hope.

refuge.answer: The most comprehensive refuge narrated is Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6369: from worry and grief, incapacity and laziness, cowardice and miserliness, the burden of debt and being overpowered by men. Eight things in four pairs, each pair placing something you cannot help beside something you can.
faq: What is the most complete duʿā of refuge?
Bukhārī 6369. Anas reports the Prophet said it constantly, and its eight items cover states, faults and pressures rather than only external threats.
What do I say for protection generally?
The perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6879, said on arriving anywhere. Surah al-Falaq and an-Nās are the other named refuges.
Is there a refuge said before sleep?
Yes. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6315 and Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5051 are both on this page with their full wording.

morning-evening.answer: Abu Bakr asked for words to say morning and evening and was given: Allāhumma fāṭira-s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ, ʿālima-l-ghaybi wa-sh-shahādah, ending with refuge from the evil of his own self. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5067. The first thing refuge is sought from is not Satan but the self.
faq: What are the morning and evening adhkār?

The core ones are on this page with their sources: Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5067, sayyid al-istighfār in Abī Dāwūd 5070, and the declaration in Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5068 that by You we enter the morning and the evening.
When exactly are they said?
After the dawn prayer and after the afternoon or sunset prayer, following the narrations. Each entry here notes the time it was said.
Which one has the strongest promise attached?
Sayyid al-istighfār: whoever says it in the day with certainty and dies before evening enters the Garden. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5070.

sleep.answer: Lying down, the Prophet said Allāhumma bismika amūtu wa aḥyā, O Allah, in Your name I die and I live. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6314. Waking, he said alḥamdu lillāhi-lladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi-n-nushūr.
faq: What duʿā do I say before sleeping?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6314 is the shortest. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6315 gives the longer surrender narrated to al-Barāʾ, and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 6892 gives the one said after shaking out the bed.
Should I recite anything from the Qurʾan?
Ayat al-Kursī and the three protective surahs are among the narrations carried here, each with its reference and grading.
What is said on waking?
Alḥamdu lillāhi-lladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi-n-nushūr, from the same narration in Bukhārī 6314.

prayer.answer: The duʿā said between the two prostrations is rabbi-ghfir lī wa-rḥamnī wa-jburnī wa-rzuqnī wa-rfaʿnī. Jabr is the word for setting a broken bone, so it asks to be put back together rather than improved. Sunan Ibn Mājah 898.
faq: What do you say in prayer besides the recitation?
This page carries the narrated supplications by position: the opening, the bowing, the prostration, between the prostrations, and after the tashahhud, each with its source.
What is the duʿā after the tashahhud?
Refuge from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, the trial of living and dying, and the false messiah. Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1324.
Where in prayer is duʿā most likely answered?
Sunan an-Nasāʾī 1137: the closest a servant comes to his Lord is while prostrating, so make much supplication then.

mosque.answer: Entering, the Prophet said rabbi-ghfir lī dhunūbī wa-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik, my Lord forgive my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy. Leaving, the same but asking for the doors of His bounty. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 314.
faq: What do you say entering a mosque?
Tirmidhī 314. Mercy is what you go in for; provision is what you go back out into, which is why the noun changes.
Is there a longer duʿā for entering?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 466 gives the refuge said on entering: in Allah the Magnificent, in His noble face and His eternal authority, from the rejected Satan.
What is the reward for building a mosque?
Sunan Ibn Mājah 738: whoever builds a mosque for Allah, even the size of a sandgrouse's scrape in the ground, Allah builds him a house in the Garden.

home.answer: Leaving the house the Prophet said bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿala-llāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5095 adds that the one who says it is told: you are guided, defended and protected. Umm Salamah says he never left without raising his eyes and asking refuge from wronging or being wronged.
faq: What do you say when leaving home?
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5095. Sunan Abī Dāwūd 5094 gives the second half of the practice: refuge from going astray or being led astray, slipping or being made to slip, wronging or being wronged.
Is there a duʿā for entering the house?
Yes, and it is carried here with its source and grading alongside the supplications for the household.
What protects a home?
The narrations on this page include the reading of Surah al-Baqarah in the house and the remembrance said on entering, each referenced.

eating.answer: The Prophet took hold of the top of a shared dish and said: eat in the name of Allah from around it and leave its top alone, for the blessing comes down onto it from above. Sunan Ibn Mājah 3276. After eating, Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3456 gives the praise said as the food is taken away.
faq: What do you say before eating?
Bismillāh, and if forgotten, bismillāhi awwalahu wa ākhirah. The narrations are on this page with references.
What do you say after eating?
Alḥamdu lillāhi ḥamdan kathīran ṭayyiban mubārakan fīh, ghayra muwaddaʿin wa lā mustaghnan ʿanhu rabbanā. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3456.
Is there guidance on how to eat from a shared plate?
Sunan Ibn Mājah 3276: from the sides, not the middle, because the blessing descends onto the top.

rain-weather.answer: When rain fell the Prophet said Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfiʿā, O Allah, a beneficial downpour. When it would not stop he did not ask for it to end but to be moved: to the ridges of the mountains, the beds of the valleys, and where the trees grow. Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik 451.
faq: What do you say when it rains?
Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfiʿā. The full narration and its source are on this page.
Is there a duʿā for drought?
Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik 450 and Sunan Abī Dāwūd 1169, which asks for rain that relieves, is wholesome, useful and not harmful, soon and not delayed.
What do you say in a storm?
Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 2252: do not curse the wind, and the wording to say instead, asking for the good of it and of what it was sent with.

evil-eye.answer: The Prophet used over Hasan and Husayn the words Ibrāhīm used over his sons: uʿīdhukumā bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah, min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3371. The third clause names the eye that harms.
faq: What protects against the evil eye?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3371, and Surah al-Falaq at Qurʾan 113, which names the envier when he envies.
Is the evil eye real in Islam?
The narrations carried here treat it as real and give the wording used against it. Every entry shows its collection, number and grading.
What do I say if I admire something?
Mā shāʾa-llāhu lā quwwata illā billāh, from Qurʾan 18:39, is the wording narrated for it and is on this page.

dhikr.answer: Two phrases are described as light on the tongue and heavy on the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: subḥāna-llāhi wa biḥamdih, subḥāna-llāhi-l-ʿaẓīm. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6406. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3517 adds that alḥamdu lillāh fills the scale.
faq: What is the best dhikr to say?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6406 names two phrases as beloved to the Most Merciful and heavy on the scale. Jāmiʿ at-Tirmidhī 3593 names subḥāna rabbī wa biḥamdih as what Allah chose for His angels.
How many times should it be said?
The narrations here give the counts where they were specified, including the hundred after prayer and the thirty-three of each before sleep, with references.
What is the shortest dhikr with the largest reward?
Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6405 records a hundred words that weigh more than they look. It is on this page in full.

misc.answer: This page collects entries that did not fall under a single situation. Each one still carries its full source and its authenticity grading, and can be searched from the home page by typing what you are actually feeling.
faq: Why is this page called misc?
These are verified entries whose subject did not map cleanly to one of the 43 situations. They are indexed here rather than left unreachable.
Are these less authentic than the others?
No. Every entry on the site passes the same rule: the Arabic must match a primary source word for word, and the hadith grading must pass before it is published.
How do I find something specific?
Type what you are feeling on the home page, or use the browse page to move through all 43 situations by category.
